raw_response:
Aiya, let me think about this year's planting...

I've been working this 9 mu most of my life, and at 70 my back isn't what it used to be. My son works at a factory in Handan and only comes home for the busy times. My daughter-in-law helps when she can, but most days it's just me and the old lady doing the work. So I can't be too ambitious.

I split the land the way I always have: 2 mu in cotton on the sandy patch, and the other 7 mu in wheat-maize like everyone else in the village. I know some young folks gave up cotton because it's too much work, and truth be told I've been thinking about it too — the picking just kills my back. But I've grown cotton my whole life, and those 2 mu are on land that doesn't do as well with wheat anyway. So I keep it.

**For wheat**, I plant around mid-October, after the first cool rain. I saved some seed from last year's harvest — it was a good crop — but I'll mix in a bag of new seed from the village shop to keep things fresh. Before planting I spread about 50 jin (25 kg) of diammonium per mu as base fertilizer. That's what old Wang down the road does and his wheat is always the best in the village. Then at green-up in early spring I topdress maybe 40 jin of urea per mu. If the wheat looks yellow at jointing I'll add a bit more, but fertilizer costs too much to waste.

I'll water the wheat 4 times from the well — before freeze-up, at green-up, at jointing, and at grain fill. The electricity isn't cheap so I don't water more than I need to. Last year I got about 900 jin per mu (that's around 450 kg), and I'd be happy with that again.

**For maize**, as soon as the combine leaves the wheat field in mid-June I rush to plant. No time to rest the soil — if you wait a week you lose too much. I buy hybrid seed from the shop, whichever one the shop owner recommends. I use no-till, just drill the maize right into the stubble. I put down urea and some compound fertilizer at sowing, then topdress more urea when the maize is knee-high. One or two waterings usually — if the summer rains come, I don't need to water at all.

**For cotton**, I plant around April 20th. I plow the 2 mu first, put on some compound fertilizer, and sow by hand. Cotton needs spraying — bollworm, aphids, whatever comes. I watch the leaves and spray when I see trouble. I topdress urea at flowering. Picking starts in September and goes on for weeks. My son tries to come home for a few days, and I'll hire a neighbor's daughter-in-law for 4 or 5 days at 120 yuan a day.

Money's always tight. I keep some cash in the drawer for emergencies — at my age you never know when you'll need the clinic.
